report:
**Conclusion:** Your view is too strong if it means “acupuncture definitely does not reduce depression symptoms in pregnancy.” One reasonably sized randomized trial found a benefit, but the overall evidence remains **insufficient to establish acupuncture as an effective treatment**.

The key 2010 trial randomly assigned 150 pregnant women with major depressive disorder to depression-specific acupuncture, control acupuncture, or massage for 8 weeks. It reported better symptom response with depression-specific acupuncture (commonly summarized as 63% versus 44% across the control treatments). This supports a *possible* effect, not a definitive one: it was a single trial, used active rather than inert controls, and subjective depression outcomes can be influenced by expectations and nonspecific therapeutic attention.  
https://journals.lww.com/greenjournal/fulltext/2010/03000/acupuncture_for_depression_during_pregnancy__a.7.aspx

Most importantly, Cochrane’s review of non-drug/non-psychological treatments for antenatal depression concluded that there was **not enough evidence** to determine whether acupuncture is effective. That is stronger and more up-to-date evidence synthesis than relying on one positive trial.  
https://www.cochrane.org/th/evidence/CD006795_interventions-other-pharmacological-psychosocial-or-psychological-treating-antenatal-depression

Major clinical guidance likewise does not present acupuncture as an established depression treatment in pregnancy. ACOG’s perinatal mental-health treatment guideline addresses evidence-based management of depression and focuses on psychotherapy and medication decisions rather than recommending acupuncture.  
https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/clinical-practice-guideline/articles/2023/06/treatment-and-management-of-mental-health-conditions-during-pregnancy-and-postpartum

So the defensible claim is: **acupuncture may help some pregnant people, but evidence is limited and uncertain; it should not replace assessment and established treatment for depression.**
